title: How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency
population: 25 experimental studies; participant characteristics are not detailed in the abstract.
key_findings: When weekly volume was equated, training a muscle more or less often per week made no significant difference to growth, including in trained participants, with direct measures, and for upper and lower body.
In studies where volume was not equated, higher frequencies were favoured, but the difference between once and three or more times a week was modest.
The authors conclude that, for a given weekly volume, frequency can follow personal preference.
methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression of weekly frequency per muscle, separating volume-equated from non-volume-equated studies.
limitations: In non-equated studies frequency and volume rise together, so their effects are confounded; the abstract does not describe the participants' age, sex or training status overall.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
